systematicSearch.scope: Exact COL26.8 accepted identity and full parent chain; one primary study of the captive pied-tamarin faecal microbiome and its association with chronic recurrent diarrhoea and weight loss.
systematicSearch.method: Resolved the accepted COL identity and every parent node by stable ID in the release-pinned search and hierarchy registries. Read the primary article abstract, sampling methods, results, discussion, limitations, and item-level license. No broad or multi-facet literature review was performed.
systematicSearch.queryOrPath: Pinned COL26.8 dataset 316115 usage 4TZBJ; Richards-Rios et al. 2021, DOI 10.1186/s42523-020-00062-4.
systematicSearch.inclusionCriteria: Exact accepted species identity and a primary article with explicit captive setting, sample, methods, outcomes, limitations, and item-level reuse license.
systematicSearch.exclusionCriteria: Name-only matches, causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations, generalization from captive to wild animals, and claims about facets not assessed by this study.

gaps: No taxon-specific morphology or diagnosis was assessed.
No development, reproduction, or survival history was assessed.

claims.text: In a single captive-colony comparison at Jersey Zoo, 16S faecal microbiome profiles from six pied tamarins classified as affected by recurrent diarrhoea and weight loss and 13 unaffected animals showed higher relative abundance of Lactobacillus amplicon sequence variants in affected animals; some Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae variants were more abundant in unaffected animals. The comparison is exploratory: only six affected samples were sequenced, affected animals were older and had substantially greater lifetime antibiotic exposure, and the study does not establish cause or describe wild populations.
claims.locator: Methods, Selection of animals and sampling; Results, Number of affected animals and Sequencing effort; Results, Differentially abundant ASVs; Discussion.
claims.placeTimeScope: Jersey Zoo, Jersey; colony sampling between November 2018 and April 2019. The article classified 8 affected and 13 unaffected animals; two affected samples lacked sufficient DNA, leaving six affected and 13 unaffected animals in the 16S analysis.
claims.lifeStatus: Captive colony animals; no wild individuals were included.

gaps: Small sample from one captive colony; affected animals differed in age and antibiotic exposure. No causal, wild-population, or across-colony inference is supported.
No phylogenetic or comparative evolutionary evidence was assessed.
No range or distribution source was independently checked; the captive study site is not a range record.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No current conservation assessment, threat analysis, or population trend was independently assessed.

reasons: One primary captive-colony microbiome study supports a single bounded, exploratory ecology claim.
Six facets remain not assessed and ecology is supported by one small study with age and antibiotic-exposure confounding.
No systematic multi-source species review or independent expert review has been completed.
